candidates.buyer: Owner-operators and small firms running water or sewage tankers, who need a permit from the regional water utility
candidates.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers (also 13 and 18)
candidates.existing: The Arabic competitor search found no Oman platform for tanker operators. Licensees (the utility operating companies) must run the electronic register and install the tracking devices, so the likely software sits with the utilities and not the operators. A Saudi 'Tasreeh' platform from National Water Company is a different country.
candidates.name: Independent water and sewage tanker operator permit and SLA compliance kit
candidates.trigger: APSR Decision 31/2025 (Gazette 1593, 27 Apr 2025, effective the next day). No tanker may operate without a permit and a signed unified SLA (Art. 2-3). Existing operators had one year, to about late Apr 2026, to comply. Colour-coding and Arabic labelling (Art. 6). Tank cleaning and disinfection, inspection and complaint records (Art. 5(5), 7). Data supplied on request (Art. 7(5)). Fines OMR 50-5,000 for individuals and OMR 500-50,000 for companies, doubled on repeat, up to OMR 50 a day (Art. 8). Muscat Municipality sewage-vehicle rules of 29 Jun 2026 add a licence plate and approved disposal points.
candidates.unchecked: Operator count and whether permits are renewed each year (the text says nothing on validity); whether operators must file periodic reports or only respond on request; whether utilities already have a portal and tracker vendors for this; the exact start of the one-year deadline; whether fines are being enforced now that the deadline has passed.

candidates.buyer: Licensed recruitment offices, which sell to households
candidates.existing: None searched; the Arabic competitor search covered only the licensing rule.
candidates.name: Recruitment office compliance kit: e-registered domestic-worker contracts, no-fee rule and worker-file archive
candidates.trigger: The domestic-worker decision (reported as MD 475/2025 or 574/2025; effective Oct 2025) requires Arabic contracts registered on the MoL platform, bans recruitment fees charged to workers, and sets 3 months to regularise. Social Development MD 405/2025 created an association of recruitment offices.
candidates.unchecked: Number of licensed offices; whether the association mandates membership or reporting; actual office-level duties (licence renewal, bank guarantee, returns); competitors; whether offices (not households) are the payers. K04 targets households through offices, this targets the offices themselves, so the buyer differs.

candidates.buyer: Small operators who rent buses and drivers to schools (22,242 school buses in Oman)
candidates.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
candidates.existing: Not searched. Naql (MTCIT) platform is the state licensing system; the education ministry is working on technology for bus safety.
candidates.name: School-bus owner and contractor compliance (vehicle operating card, bus age, driver eligibility, renewals)
candidates.trigger: Ministry of Education regulation of rented school buses (2020): valid registration and vehicle operating card from MTCIT, bus age at most 12 years, driver Omani aged 23-60 with 5 years' experience; operators told to follow rules each new academic year (Oman Observer, Oct 2026).
candidates.unchecked: Whether the rules above are still current; contract and payment process with schools; tracker or tender-portal systems; competitor search not run (budget). Whether the buyer group is mostly Omani owner-drivers with a few vehicles.

candidates.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
candidates.existing: Tracker vendors exist in the Gulf generally (not searched in Oman); Naql is the state platform.
candidates.name: Goods-vehicle tracking and licence compliance for small trucking owners
candidates.trigger: Carriage by Land executive regulation amendments (MTCIT, 2023): tracking systems required for goods transport licensees; tampering fined, licence cancelled on the third offence. Naql platform for licences.
candidates.unchecked: Whether a reporting duty exists beyond installing the device; vendor coverage; likely already served by hardware tracker sellers.

candidates.buyer: Private nurseries (355 in mid-2024, with 8,706 children)

candidates.name: Private nursery (daycare) licence and renewal file
candidates.trigger: Social Development ministerial decision 48/2017: application fee OMR 10; licence and renewal OMR 100 a year for individuals, OMR 200 for companies. The minister was reported studying home-nursery licensing.
candidates.unchecked: Recurring reports to the ministry; inspections; whether the 2017 rules were replaced; competitor tools (childcare management apps).

candidates.trigger: Wells and Aflaj regulation MD 264/2000, amended by MD 193/2023: contractors register and are classified; wells need registration and licences. 151 contractor applications and 3,990 well licence applications in 2024.
candidates.unchecked: Whether contractors file per-well completion reports; number of registered contractors; app usage.

candidates.trigger: Pesticide Law RD 64/2006; MD 41/2012; MD 160/2023 (List A banned, holders dispose within 6 months; List B restricted); regular ministry inspections.
candidates.unchecked: Any sales or stock register duty (none found); shop count.

candidates.trigger: 2022 activity regulation: 1-year licence, OMR 300 fee, renewal 30 days before expiry, at least 400 m2 site; ban on scrap collection in residential areas with OMR 500 fine; Dhofar scrap order 2013.
candidates.unchecked: Issuing authority of the 2022 rule; transaction register duty (none found); number of yards.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: New domestic-worker decision (reported as MD 475/2025 or 574/2025, number conflicting; in force from about 9-13 Oct 2025): Arabic contracts registered electronically on MoL platform, no recruitment fees charged to workers, 12h/day cap, 21 days leave, records kept 1 year after service, 3-month transition, under-21 ban. Nothing new beyond K04 for households.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: 2022 activity-licence regulation (1-year licence, OMR 300 fee, 30-day renewal notice, 400 m2 site, concrete floor, governorate approves; issuing body not confirmed); Dhofar scrap order 2013; ban on scrap collection in residential areas with OMR 500 fine; Environment Authority 2021 waste-export rules. No register or report duty found. Weak.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Oman regime found for pawnbrokers or purchase registers on second-hand goods. Only used-car selling permit rules (Muscat Municipality 2018; Sohar order 2019 limiting to industrial areas, OMR 100 fine). Unverified.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K05. Precious metals and stones AML supervision regulation exists (Gazette issue 1473, text garbled, date unconfirmed); Royal Decree 30/2016 is the AML law.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: NCSI figures via Oman Daily: about 1,527 vehicle-parts establishments to end Apr 2024, of which 671 retail used parts. No licensing, register or environmental take-back rule found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Only a camel digital ID / microchip plan (Oman Observer, undated) and Muscat Municipality abattoir hours. No mandatory trader register found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Municipal abattoirs (Muscat Municipality) serve individuals and meat shops; no private abattoir or butcher reporting duty found. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Only 2016 ministerial decisions (194/2016 ban on exporting Omani bee breeds, fine OMR 500-1000; 209/2016 hive movement ban, expired) and a subsidised hive programme. No beekeeper register or health certificate rule found. Tiny market. Weak.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Vet Practice Law RD 22/2017 with regulation MD 23/2021 (ministry register, licence renewal); Veterinary Preparations Law RD 34/2017 with regulation MD 60/2023 and fee decision MD 67/2023 (Gazette 1485, 19 Mar 2023). No record-keeping duty details seen; group is small. Weak/unverified.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Wells and Aflaj regulation MD 264/2000 amended by MD 193/2023: contractors must register and are classified by capacity. About 6,660 water licences to end-2024, of which 3,990 well licences, 2,280 well registrations, 151 drilling-contractor applications. Small buyer group, ministry-run process.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: APSR Decision 31/2025 licensing independent water/wastewater tanker operators (see candidate C1). Muscat Municipality sewage-vehicle health rules published 29 Jun 2026. Be'ah holds the municipal waste monopoly; governorates taking over container collection from 1 Dec (year unconfirmed). No septage manifest found.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Occupational safety regulation (2008, amended by MoL MD 4/2021): boilers tested every 12 months, steam and air receivers every 24 months by a competent person, with a register of test date, technician and remarks (Curtis blog 2016, current force unconfirmed). No Oman lift-inspection source found. Weak.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Water and Wastewater Sector Regulation Law RD 40/2023 (6-month transition for regulated activities, extendable 6 months). Covered through the tanker candidate C1; no separate private small-system reporting duty found.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Pesticide Law RD 64/2006; regulation MD 41/2012; MD 160/2023 replaced the lists with List A (prohibited, holders must dispose within 6 months) and List B (restricted). The ministry issued 225 retail fertiliser sale licences and 96 pesticide registration certificates in one year (year unconfirmed); North Batinah ran 6,097 inspection visits. No mandatory sales register found. Weak.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Social Development MD 405/2025 (20 Nov 2025) created an association of recruitment offices; the new domestic-worker decision bans recruitment fees and requires e-registered contracts. Office licensing rules and office count not found. See candidate C2.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Interior Ministry cemetery regulation, Gazette 1544 (2024): municipality permits cemeteries and keeps the grave register; death report needed for burial. Municipal function, no private funeral-service licensing regime found. Not a software buyer.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Ministry of Social Development supervises 173 associations (68 Omani Women's Association branches, 42 charities, 40 professional, 23 expatriate community clubs; Oman Daily 2024). A Civil Society Institutions Law with exemptions was reported by Al Rai (date unconfirmed); annual audited accounts reviewed by the ministry under the 2001 law. Small, institutional buyers. Weak. No halal supervision body found.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: 22,242 school buses (Oman Observer, 13 Sep 2026); rented school buses need a vehicle operating card, a maximum age of 12 years, and drivers aged 23-60 with 5 years' experience. Carriage by Land regulation amended 2023: tracking systems required for goods carriers; MTCIT Naql platform for licences. Taxis stay rejected (K13). See candidates C3 and C4.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money Services Business regulation published Apr 2024 (CBO) covers exchange houses, but they are few and licensed. Market traders and street vendors were not searched, so that part is not_reached.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Nurseries: 355 nurseries, 8,706 children (mid-2024); Social Development ministerial decision 48/2017 sets fees (OMR 100 a year individuals, OMR 200 companies); the minister was reported studying home nursery licensing (date unknown). Driving schools: Royal Oman Police 2024 regulation covers instruction offences (age 18, no night lessons 22:00-06:00). Tattoo studios, food producers and hunting outfitters not searched.
